title: What people frame, ii
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Wednesday: a fishing license, expired 1988. The man wants it framed with the fine. 'Both. Same frame.'

panels.composition: The counter. A MAN in waders, dripping, with a fishing license and a folded pink citation.

balloons.text: License. And the ticket. Same frame.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, a man in dripping waders at a frame-shop counter laying down a fishing license and a folded pink citation, a young clerk

panels.composition: The two documents on the counter. The license: 1988. The citation: 1988, the day after it expired. $45.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, close-up of a 1988 fishing license and a pink citation dated the day after it expired lying side by side on a counter

panels.composition: Wood cutting a two-window mat. The Owner, from the back, not looking up.

balloons.text: Two windows, Arthur. Ticket on top.
I'm telling you anyway. It's the good one.

image.notes: 'Arthur' — the owner's first of two in eleven years.

panels.composition: The framed pair on the counter. The man looking at his own ticket under glass with enormous satisfaction.
